display.purpose: Topic titles on the Learn sheet. The largest type in the product.

page-title.purpose: H1 on every top-level view. No eyebrow label above it.

readout.purpose: The mono voice: counts, dates, positions, status words, track labels, kickers. Everything the instrument reports rather than says.

shadows.name: edge
shadows.purpose: The lit top edge on anything raised. Paired with edge-under.

shadows.name: edge-under
shadows.purpose: The dark lower lip that gives a raised control thickness.

shadows.name: engrave
shadows.purpose: Anything cut into the chassis: inputs, progress tracks, an engaged filter chip.

shadows.name: press
shadows.purpose: A held control dropping into the chassis.

shadows.name: press-lit
shadows.purpose: The same press read on the polished primary, which needs far less black in it to look held.

shadows.name: ambient-panel
shadows.purpose: Reserved for the flashcard and the due-Test surface — the single most important element per view.

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Default duration for hover/focus/active feedback on buttons, chips, fields, nav.

motion.name: reduced-motion-floor
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion collapses all animation/transition durations to near-zero.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single accent-colored action per screen — Start due Test, Save topic, Begin session.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { min-height: 44px; padding: 11px 14px; border-radius: 10px; border: 1px solid #e9edf3; background: #e9edf3; color: #0b0d10; font: 700 0.86rem ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.18s ease, border-color 0.18s ease, transform 0.18s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #ffffff; border-color: #ffffff; } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid rgba(255,255,255,.4); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Secondary action, same shape as primary, a milled-grey bevel instead of the polish.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { min-height: 44px; padding: 11px 14px; border-radius: 10px; border: 1px solid #3d4450; background: #1d2126; color: #e6eaf0; font: 700 0.86rem ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.18s ease, border-color 0.18s ease; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { background: #272c33; border-color: #5b6472; } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid rgba(255,255,255,.4); outline-offset: 2px; border-color: #e9edf3; }

components.name: Filter Chip
components.description: Track/status filter. Active state reuses the same polish-equals-current logic as buttons and nav.
components.css: .ds-chip { min-height: 38px; padding: 8px 11px; border-radius: 999px; border: 1px solid #343a42; background: transparent; color: #e6eaf0; font: 700 0.76rem ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.18s ease, border-color 0.18s ease, color 0.18s ease; } .ds-chip:hover { border-color: #3d4450; } .ds-chip-active, .ds-chip[aria-pressed="true"] { background: #e9edf3; border-color: #e9edf3; color: #0b0d10; } .ds-chip:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid rgba(255,255,255,.4); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Text Field
components.description: Search and form input. One step darker than surrounding surfaces for contrast.
components.css: .ds-field { min-height: 44px; width: 100%; padding: 11px 12px; border-radius: 10px; border: 1px solid #3d4450; background: #0b0d10; color: #e6eaf0; font: 400 0.86rem ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif; } .ds-field::placeholder { color: #767f8e; } .ds-field:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid rgba(255,255,255,.4); outline-offset: 2px; border-color: #e9edf3; }

components.name: Topic Row
components.description: A dense index row, deliberately not a card. Trailing chevron and hairline divider signal affordance instead of shadow/lift.
components.css: .ds-topic-row { position: relative; display: block; width: 100%; text-align: left; border: 0; border-bottom: 1px solid #343a42; border-radius: 0; padding: 15px 24px 15px 2px; background: transparent; color: #e6eaf0; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.18s ease, padding 0.18s ease; } .ds-topic-row:hover { background: rgba(255,255,255,.018); padding-inline: 10px; } .ds-topic-row::after { content: '\203A'; position: absolute; right: 5px; top: 50%; transform: translateY(-50%); color: #868f9d; font-size: 1.2rem; } .ds-topic-top { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: baseline; gap: 8px; padding-right: 20px; } .ds-topic-title { margin: 0; font: 700 0.98rem ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-topic-scope { max-width: 68ch; font-size: 0.77rem; color: #979fac; margin: 4px 0 10px; } .ds-meta-row { display: flex; gap: 6px; } .ds-tag { font-size: 0.72rem; color: #868f9d; } .ds-tag + .ds-tag::before { content: '\00b7'; color: #5b6472; margin-right: 6px; } .ds-status-dot { display: inline-block; width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 50%; background: #92b5ae; margin-right: 5px; } .ds-topic-row:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid rgba(255,255,255,.4); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Nav Item
components.description: Bottom nav on mobile, left rail on desktop. Active state uses Highlight, aria-current=page.
components.html: <button class="ds-nav-btn ds-nav-btn-active" aria-current="page" aria-label="Library"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" width="22" height="22"><path d="M4 5.5A2.5 2.5 0 0 1 6.5 3H20v16H6.5A2.5 2.5 0 0 0 4 21.5v-16Z" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.7"/><path d="M4 18.5A2.5 2.5 0 0 1 6.5 16H20" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.7"/></svg>Library</button>
components.css: .ds-nav-btn { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; gap: 3px; min-height: 50px; padding: 6px 10px; border: 0; border-radius: 9px; background: transparent; color: #979fac; font: 700 0.66rem ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: color 0.18s ease, background 0.18s ease; } .ds-nav-btn:hover { color: #e6eaf0; } .ds-nav-btn-active, .ds-nav-btn[aria-current='page'] { color: #ffffff; background: rgba(255,255,255,.07); } .ds-nav-btn:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid rgba(255,255,255,.4); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Sheet Close Button
components.description: 44x44px dismiss control on modal sheets. Always carries an explicit aria-label naming what it closes.
components.html: <button class="ds-close-btn" aria-label="Close topic details"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" width="18" height="18"><path d="M6 6l12 12M18 6L6 18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.8" stroke-linecap="round"/></svg></button>
components.css: .ds-close-btn { width: 44px; height: 44px; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; border: 1px solid #343a42; border-radius: 10px; background: #1d2126; color: #e6eaf0; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.18s ease, border-color 0.18s ease; } .ds-close-btn:hover { background: #272c33; border-color: #3d4450; } .ds-close-btn:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid rgba(255,255,255,.4); outline-offset: 2px; border-color: #e9edf3; }

narrative.overview: Argus is styled as a precision instrument, not a dashboard and not a journal: a dark, low-glare index the owner opens for a few minutes, uses without friction, and closes. Surfaces are milled cool grey and read as stamped plate; controls protrude with a lit top edge and fall into the chassis when held; progress tracks are cut into the surface rather than drawn on it. One thing on a screen is polished, and it is the action you are being asked to take. A native sans carries everything a person reads and operates; a native mono carries everything the instrument reports.
keyCharacteristics: Cool milled greys over grain, machining marks and a convex highlight; one polished-steel accent, never decorative
Sans for language, mono for readings, and the boundary between them is meaningful
Depth from bevel and engraving, not from stacked drop shadows
Exactly one warm colour in the product, and it means a skill has decayed
Dense index rows over card grids; a topic list reads like a table of contents
Motion is state feedback plus one piece of card physics; nothing else moves

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: The polish (near-white steel) appears only on the primary action, the current selection, and active state. If a second element on the same screen carries it, one of them is wrong. The accent is a material rather than a hue: --ink is deliberately held below white so the two separate.

rules.name: The No Track-as-Background Rule
rules.body: Learning/Survival/Tradecraft colors label metadata (a tag, a dot) and are never used as a card background, button fill, or large surface area, that would tip the product toward the tactical/game aesthetic it explicitly rejects.

rules.name: The No-Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: Page and section headings do not get an eyebrow label above them. Eyebrow-weight type is reserved for genuine metadata, never as heading decoration.

rules.name: The Bevel-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Depth on ordinary controls comes from the bevel — a lit top edge and a dark lower lip — and on recessed elements from an inset engraving. Drop shadow is spent once, on the single most important surface per view.

rules.name: The Nothing-Nests Rule
rules.body: A card does not contain another card. If a component needs internal grouping, use a hairline divider or spacing, not a nested bordered container.

rules.name: The One Warm Colour Rule
rules.body: Tarnish (#d68d5e) is the only warm colour in the product and it means exactly one thing: this skill has decayed and needs repair. On an otherwise entirely grey-and-white screen it cannot be missed. Spending it anywhere else destroys the only pre-attentive signal the system has.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Mono means a reading; sans means language. A button verb never uses the mono, and a status word never uses the sans. Mixing them destroys the only signal that tells the eye which is which.

dos: Do open every top-level view on the task (what's due, start Test), never on a summary, pitch, or hero.
Do hold the polish to exactly three roles: primary action, current selection, active/current state.
Do build hierarchy from tonal layering and bevel, and reserve drop shadow for the one lit surface per view.
Do render topic listings as a dense hairline-divided index, not a card grid.
Do give every interactive element default, hover, focus-visible, active, and disabled states, with a minimum 44px primary touch target.
Do name controls as direct actions and explain the recovery path in empty states.
Do treat retention decay as a routing signal, same visual weight as any other status, never styled as an error or a scolding.
Do keep JSON export/import visually first-class, not buried as a settings afterthought.
Do keep tarnish for decay alone, so it stays the one warm thing on a cool screen.
Do set every reading — count, date, position, status, track — in the mono voice, and everything a person reads or presses in the sans.
donts: Don't put a hero, oversized slogan, or eyebrow label above a page or section heading.
Don't build a wall of identical metric cards; consolidate into one instrument-panel stat strip.
Don't nest a card inside a card, or use border-left/border-right as a colored accent stripe on any row, alert, or callout.
Don't use gradient text, glassmorphism, or decorative rings/gradients anywhere in the Test loop.

Don't let the machined material drag the language tactical. The chassis is machined; the words are not — Argus says 'Needs repair' and 'Start', never 'TST' or 'INITIATE EXECUTION'. The subject matter invites the opposite, and the framing is competence, not catastrophe.
Don't add streaks, badges, XP, or any shame-based nudge for missed Test days.
Don't widen the mobile layout for desktop and call it done; desktop gets a genuine side-rail, task-oriented layout.
Don't use a serif or fluid display typeface; display character comes from size, weight and tracking.
Don't add outer glow. A polished surface catches light; it does not emit it, and glow smears on OLED.
